chunks: Ahmad ibn Hilal, al-Abartai, Abu Ja'far.

I regard halting (to be appropriate) in regards to his hadith, except for what he narrates from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from the book 'al-Mashikhah' and Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from his 'Nawadir'. The venerable of the Asahb al-Hadith have heard these two books and relied upon what is in them. He was born in the year 180, and died in the year 267.

key_terms.التَّوَقُّف: Halting or suspending judgment regarding the reliability of a narrator or their hadith.
key_terms.النَّوَادِر: A specific book of rare narrations by Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr.
key_terms.الْمَشِيخَة: A specific book of narrations by al-Hasan ibn Mahbub.

ai.seo_question: What is the status of Ahmad ibn Hilal's hadith in Shia scholarship?
ai.summary: This biographical entry discusses Ahmad ibn Hilal al-Abartai, a narrator whose hadith are generally regarded with caution (tawaffuf) due to potential weaknesses, with specific exceptions for narrations transmitted from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub and Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr. These specific works were validated by the prominent scholars of hadith who relied upon them. The text concludes with his birth and death years.
